assessments.reasoning: The Creative Commons legal-tools repository at commit 91780e140892982eb3e0d530591ccbbca0d4690d supplies the title and operative sections 2 and 3. The captured full-file digest matches the claim’s representation digest a2010f343487d3f7618affe54f789f5487602331c0a8d03f49e9a7c547cf0499.

The official creativecommons.org plaintext returned the same title, 7,048-byte length and full-file SHA-256 as the pinned plaintext. This checks the publisher route at retrieval. Both copies share publisher authority.

The README at the same Creative Commons commit places the CC0 example under Public Domain Tools. It specifies category publicdomain, title CC0 1.0 Universal, identifier CC0 1.0, unit zero, version 1.0, Universal scope and language en. Its separate Vocabulary notice documents use for code.

License Index SCOPE.md at cdff8aeed68bf1f9c62d8c86159c7dc08b2d75d7 defines a related legal instrument as “A distinct dedication, mark, notice, or conditional term with a documented connection to software licensing.” CC0 meets the dedication branch. The document assigns the data model and crosswalk decisions to the Index and distinguishes discovery, acceptance and qualified selection. It supplies the criterion, while the supplied mapping carries the value active.

challenge.method: Read section 3 against section 2 to test whether the fallback has an independent trigger, edition or identity. Compared the publisher’s namespace entry, its Vocabulary code dedication, SPDX’s license-list treatment and the Index’s admission criteria to determine which source supports each part of the mapping.
challenge.results: Section 3 expressly depends on the judgment about the section 2 waiver and dates the fallback license to the application of CC0. Both provisions belong to one titled instrument. The namespace entry establishes the general identity. The Vocabulary dedication documents a connection to software licensing, but could not by itself identify the general reference edition. SPDX controls its own list kind. The Index controls the related-instrument classification and the entity lifecycle. The inspected sources disclose no conflict within those scopes.

limitations: The scope is the identified English reference edition. Establishing the status of a particular work requires evidence of application, the Affirmer’s rights and the relevant law.
Active describes the value assigned by the entity mapping. Existing admission on main and selection in a qualified release would require separate registry evidence.
The policy documents were inspected at the specified commit. The bundle digest was supplied with the task and was not independently recomputed.
reasoning: Creative Commons identifies the English edition as CC0 1.0 Universal and classifies it as a public domain tool. Section 2 waives the Affirmer’s rights to the extent permitted by applicable law. Section 3 preserves as much of that waiver as the law permits and grants a license to each affected person to the extent the waiver is judged invalid or ineffective. The Index’s related-instrument criterion fits this distinct dedication. Creative Commons documents both its general identity and an instance of its use for software. The supplied entity mapping assigns the lifecycle value active. Before inspecting these sources, I read the complete SCES-1.0 Evidence Standard, Codex Research Protocol and research task brief, in that order, at commit ab26f278422772f2d9e5d4dd016407d14372a710. The supplied adopted bundle SHA-256 is 14da3f31f697ab828d4a4560f060dbe511861020db54bea7bc531e20ea0855ce. Standard §4 and protocol stage 7 require fresh source inspection and a targeted challenge to identity merges. I applied that requirement to the proposed boundary between the waiver and fallback.
